title.official: Questioning of class and subclass members

operative_text.controlling:
2.8(1)  If under section 18(2) of the Class Proceedings Act the
Court requires a class member or subclass member to file and serve
an affidavit of records, the Court may do either or both of the
following:
(a) limit the purpose and scope of the records to be produced
and of questioning;
(b) determine how the evidence obtained may be used.
(2)  If a class member or subclass member is questioned under
section 18(2) of the Class Proceedings Act, the Court may do either
or both of the following:
(a) limit the purpose and scope of the questioning;
(b) determine how the evidence obtained may be used.

BOOK_A.title: Questioning of Class and Subclass Members
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 5.1(2) (directions regarding discovery) ; 5.3 (modifying discovery) ; 5.5 (production of records) ; 5.17 (examination for discovery) ; 5.19 (limiting questions).
BOOK_A.commentary:
In a class action, there is no general right to pre-certiﬁcation disclosure, which would be too
slow and too much work; the court must be shown that such disclosure is necessary.⁴

Generally speaking, no discovery (questioning) is open pending a motion to certify a class
action?¹
But before any application to certify a suit as a class action, an examination for discovery
is possible and its questions can include topics relevant and material to certiﬁcation, such as
the number of tenants (said to have been all harmed).²
But the court can give directions to ﬁll in
various procedural gaps or ﬂaws before the ﬁnal decision on certiﬁcation.³
In a new action, intended ultimately to be certiﬁed as a class action, the plaintiff unsuccessfully
sought huge production of records by the defendant government.⁴
On examination for discovery of a defendant in a proposed class action by a class, before an
application to certify, see the Schneider decision.⁵
As merits of a class action are not gone into very deeply on a certiﬁcation motion, and discovery
is not usually ordered at that stage, a high executive little involved and living outside Alberta was
not ordered to give information under R.6.22.⁶
Pending a motion to certify the suit (over pensions) as a class action, the defendants need not
ﬁle statements of defence, but the defendants could ﬁle afﬁdavits responding to the certiﬁcation
motion.⁷

information_notes.text:
Section 18(2) of the Class Proceedings Act reads:
(2) After discovery of the representative plaintiff or, in a proceeding referred to in section
7, one or more of the representative plaintiffs, a defendant may, with leave of the Court,
discover other class members or subclass members..
